title: A clearer report review experience

sections.title: Make navigation part of the content

steps.text:
### Keep the explanation in focus

Readers should be able to follow a change without sorting through a toolbar of identifiers. The section title provides a stable destination, while each step has a light gray LINK on the right.

Select a few words in this paragraph, then try the LINK on its right. The link should be easy to find without competing with the explanation.

steps.text:
### Separate folding from navigation

Use the arrow and number to collapse this section. Clicking its title should navigate instead. These actions need different hit areas so a reader can copy a title or follow a link without accidentally hiding the report.

- Section title: navigate to this section.
- Arrow and number: expand or collapse.
- Paragraph anchor: share one step.

Try all three after scrolling down and returning to this section.
The same placement should work across multiple files. Compare the two file headers below and check that the explanation still feels connected to its code.

sections.title: Keep longer explanations readable on narrow screens

steps.text:
A report often needs more than one sentence to explain why a change matters. Long paragraphs are useful here because they reveal whether the anchor steals space, whether text wraps cleanly, and whether the content starts at a consistent position.

The layout should remain readable when a desktop window is narrowed to phone width. Inline code such as `resolveProjectConfiguration(workspaceRoot)` can be wider than ordinary words, and should not push the controls outside the viewport.

> This blockquote is another content shape to review. It should keep its own indentation while the step anchor remains aligned with the beginning of the step.

A final paragraph gives us enough content to check spacing before the next code block.
This intentionally longer diff lets you test navigation after scrolling well below the section heading.

After following its link, collapse this section and open the same URL again to check that the destination becomes visible.

sections.title: Handle long section titles without crowding the fold control or making the entire heading behave like a toggle

steps.text:
### Final review

This final section is deliberately far from the top. Use it to test a copied link in a new tab, browser Back and Forward, and the sticky navigation while scrolling.

1. Select and copy part of this title.
2. Open a step anchor in a new tab.
3. Collapse and expand using only the arrow and number.
4. Resize the viewport and check the same controls again.

summary:
A longer sample for reviewing navigation, readable explanations, and code changes before release. Scroll through multiple sections and try the section titles and step anchors.

This is sample content for layout review, not a description of shipped changes.
